blocks.text: West Vancouver Homes: streets and boundaries

items.t: The District of West Vancouver stretches along 28 kilometres of shoreline and up the slopes of Hollyburn Ridge.
The District was incorporated on March 15, 1912, taking jurisdiction over what had been part of the District of North Vancouver.
Ambleside is the Municipal Town Centre; the other local commercial centres are Dundarave, Caulfeild and Horseshoe Bay, plus the Park Royal regional shopping centre.
Marine Drive is the east-west waterfront road linking Ambleside, Dundarave and Horseshoe Bay; Highway 1 (Trans-Canada Highway) runs on the upper bench above it.

blocks.text: West Vancouver Homes: the housing stock

items.t: The first Official Community Plan (OCP), under the Town Planning Act of 1926, banned new industry and called for building lots larger than elsewhere in the Lower Mainland.
Ambleside was an early subdivision built on a gridiron plan with a commercial strip along Marine Drive.
In 1959, 20 hectares were rezoned permitting dozens of high-density apartment buildings in Ambleside and Hollyburn, which is why apartments concentrate there.
Altamont, built as car ownership spread after 1945, has large lots, mature trees and narrow roads giving homes the feel of country estates.
Caulfeild was laid out as an English-style village following the contours of nature, including paths of animals.

blocks.text: West Vancouver Homes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The current OCP is Bylaw No. 4985, 2018, with local area plan boundaries for Ambleside Town Centre, Horseshoe Bay, Taylor Way and the Marine Drive corridor shown in its schedules.

The Province directed the District in July 2025 to amend its OCP to increase density in the Park Royal-Taylor Way area and beside Ambleside and Dundarave, and to adopt the Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan, each by December 31, 2025.
West Vancouver delivered 58 of its 220 net-new units Year 1 housing target, per the Province.

blocks.text: West Vancouver Homes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Dundarave's name and Caulfeild's unusual spelling both come from early residents: Caulfeild is named for Francis William Caulfeild, with that spelling.
John Lawson Park in Ambleside is named for one of West Vancouver's founders.
Property tax notices are mailed in May and due the first business day in July; the District states this year's payment is due Thursday, July 2, 2026.
Metered utility statements are mailed four times a year for water, sewer (sanitary and storm) and curbside recycling, yard trimmings and garbage.
West Vancouver water is metered, so water and sewer charges depend on how much water a home uses.
A separate North Shore Wastewater Treatment Plant levy appears on the property tax bill from 2025, about $177 for a single-family home assessed at $3.66 million.

blocks.text: West Vancouver Homes: development and new projects

items.t: Park Royal-Taylor Way density: the Province directed OCP amendments for increased density in this area by December 31, 2025.
Cypress Village and Cypress West are shown as planning areas in the OCP schedules, in the Upper Lands above Highway 1.

blocks.text: West Vancouver Homes: costs and taxes

items.t: District property taxes pay for parks and streets, library, police and fire services, per the District.

Utility fees are billed quarterly for water, sewer and curbside pickup; the District's 2025 insert states projected water funding needs rose 4.5 percent and sewer and storm drainage needs rose 9.6 percent in 2025.
The District of West Vancouver is a designated taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax (SVT).

blocks.text: West Vancouver Homes: getting around

items.t: Lions Gate Bridge connects West Vancouver to Vancouver via Park Royal and Taylor Way; the Spirit Trail greenway is planned as a continuous flat connection between Lions Gate Bridge and Horseshoe Bay.
Horseshoe Bay terminal serves BC Ferries routes to Departure Bay, Langdale and Bowen Island — confirm sailings on the BC Ferries schedule pages before travel.
Highway 1 westbound ends at Horseshoe Bay, so ferry traffic and local traffic share that corridor.

blocks.text: West Vancouver Homes: risks and due diligence

items.t: The OCP schedules map natural environmental resources, steep Upper Lands and creek areas; check a lot against OCP Maps 13 (Natural Environmental Resources) and 8 (Upper Lands Planning Framework).
Homes up Hollyburn Ridge sit on slopes above Highway 1, so slope and drainage review is part of due diligence for upper lots — the District history describes development up those slopes.

blocks.text: Jared's take on West Vancouver

West Vancouver is a set of separate pockets rather than one market: Ambleside’s beach and seawall, Dundarave village on Marine Drive, Horseshoe Bay at the ferry terminal and the British Properties above. Each one draws a different buyer.
